title: Customer Package-to-Booking UX
outcome: A customer can move from a published package detail into a traveller-specific booking plan in a few clear steps while preserving authoritative occupancy, pricing, availability and customer-shell consistency.
actor: Public or authenticated NoorPath customer evaluating a published Umrah departure.
modules: Catalogue remains authoritative for published package and departure facts.
Pricing remains authoritative for occupancy prices and quote totals.
Inventory remains authoritative for effective availability and holds.
Travellers remains authoritative for account-owned traveller identity.
Booking consumes the selected departure, occupancy, travellers, price version and inventory references without inventing commercial state in the UI.
routes: Plan journey -> Sign in when required
Plan journey -> Select or add travellers
Plan journey -> Review quote -> Secure availability
Customer pages -> consistent NoorPath customer shell and footer
acceptance: Package detail exposes available occupancy options as an explicit customer choice rather than a passive price list only.
Unavailable occupancy remains visibly unavailable and cannot be selected.
The selected occupancy carries into the plan journey route and is restored only when it remains saleable.
Package and plan pages use the shared customer shell without duplicate legacy headers or footers.
Customers always have a deterministic route back to package context during planning.
The existing quote, inventory hold, traveller ownership and authentication boundaries remain unchanged.
Total, due-now, remaining balance and instalment information remain authoritative and are shown before commitment.
Loading, unavailable, error, unauthenticated and retry states remain complete.
Desktop and mobile layouts preserve the approved NoorPath Package visual language with WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard access, visible focus, 44px minimum targets and reduced-motion support.
Rendered and navigation E2E coverage verifies package -> plan and back navigation without dead ends.
exclusions: Operator package-authoring drag and drop, icon picking or smart inclusion defaults.
Operator/admin shell alignment and staff portal extraction.
New pricing, inventory, payment or booking policies.
